description: Individually inspected complete source text and rendered figures; original adapted text-only practice and independently checked answers. No original sitting, official answer key, publisher licence, or question number asserted.

records.source_observation: Source gives circular area increasing at 1.5 square centimetres per second and asks for radial growth when area is 2 square centimetres, to three significant figures.
records.adapted_prompt: The area of a circular region increases at 1.5 cm² per second. When its area is 2 cm², how fast is its radius increasing, to three significant figures?

records.source_observation: Rendered figure shows S outside the circle, SP and SR tangent at P and R, angle PSR 36 degrees, and Q on the major arc PR. The source prose incorrectly places S on the circumference; the figure fixes the geometry.

source_figure.transcription: Circle centre C. Tangents from the exterior point S meet the circle at P and R. The angle between the tangent segments at S is 36 degrees. Point Q lies on the major arc from P to R, so angle PQR subtends the minor arc PR.

records.adapted_prompt: From a point S outside a circle, tangents SP and SR touch it at P and R. If ∠PSR=36° and Q is on the major arc PR, what is ∠PQR?

records.source_observation: Source equation is log(y+8)+log(y−8)=2log3+2log5. Its displayed ±17 answer omits the domain y>8; the adapted choices distinguish the sole real solution.
records.adapted_prompt: For real y, solve log₁₀(y+8)+log₁₀(y−8)=2log₁₀3+2log₁₀5. Which value satisfies the equation?

records.source_observation: Source states eight red balls, a white draw half as likely as a red draw, and two draws without replacement. Its posted 8/33 answer counts only red then white; the adapted question explicitly includes either order.
records.adapted_prompt: A bag has eight red balls and some white balls. On one draw, a white ball is half as likely as a red ball. If two balls are drawn without replacement, what is the probability of one red and one white in either order?

records.source_observation: Rendered bar chart shows percentage bands 0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100 with respective student counts 3, 5, 3, 8. The source asks for the number scoring at least 25 percent.

source_figure.transcription: Four percentage-score bars are labelled 0–25, 25–50, 50–75 and 75–100. Their heights on the frequency axis are respectively 3, 5, 3 and 8 students. The at-least-25-percent count is the sum of the final three bars.

records.adapted_prompt: A class has 3 students in the score band [0%,25%), 5 in [25%,50%), 3 in [50%,75%), and 8 in [75%,100%]. How many scored at least 25%?

records.source_observation: Rendered triangle labels A 82 degrees, C 56 degrees and side CB 43.2 cm. The requested side AB is opposite C.

source_figure.transcription: Triangle ABC has angle A marked 82 degrees and angle C marked 56 degrees. The side CB opposite A is labelled 43.2 centimetres. The unknown side AB is opposite C.

records.adapted_prompt: In triangle ABC, ∠A=82°, ∠C=56°, and BC=43.2 cm. Find AB to three significant figures.

records.source_observation: Rendered diagram labels circle radius 13 cm and chord AB 24 cm, and asks for minor arc AB to three significant figures.

source_figure.transcription: Circle with centre O, radius OB marked 13 centimetres, and chord AB marked 24 centimetres. The minor arc between A and B is the requested length.

records.adapted_prompt: A circle has radius 13 cm and a chord 24 cm long. Find the length of the minor arc subtended by this chord, to three significant figures.

records.source_observation: The visible source terms are 16.54×10⁻⁵−6.76×10⁻⁸+0.23×10⁻⁶. Exact arithmetic gives 1.655624×10⁻⁴; the earlier held audit miscomputed it. The adapted prompt states three-significant-figure rounding explicitly.
records.adapted_prompt: Evaluate 16.54×10⁻⁵ − 6.76×10⁻⁸ + 0.23×10⁻⁶. Give the result in standard form to three significant figures.

records.source_observation: Rendered L-shaped prism has constant 6 cm width, a lower 8 cm-high beam extending 26 cm to the upright, a final 10 cm upright length, and a total upright height of 22 cm.

source_figure.transcription: Isometric L-shaped solid. Front rectangular cross-section is 6 centimetres wide and 8 centimetres high. Its horizontal run to the taller section is labelled 26 centimetres. The tall end is another 10 centimetres long in the same direction and has total height 22 centimetres. The entire solid has width 6 centimetres.

records.adapted_prompt: An L-shaped solid has a constant width of 6 cm. Its lower beam is 36 cm long and 8 cm high. Over the final 10 cm of its length, the solid rises to a total height of 22 cm. What is its volume?
